title: How well does AI speak your language?
gist: World Bank economist Daniel Gerszon Mahler shows AI training data is starkly skewed toward languages of wealthy countries — English alone is nearly half of global URLs, Danish is ~7x overrepresented online relative to its speaker base, while Punjabi (hundreds of millions of speakers) is roughly 250x underrepresented — meaning generative AI will systematically underperform for lower-income-country languages absent deliberate data investment.

themes.theme: AI Training Data Is Skewed Toward Rich-Country Languages

insights.claim: English alone accounts for nearly half of all URLs on the global internet, meaning large language models trained on web-scraped text are disproportionately built on English-language material.
insights.speaker: Daniel Gerszon Mahler
insights.so_what: A structural data asymmetry underlying every major LLM — relevant to evaluating model quality claims for non-English, low-resource-language deployments.
insights.quote: English alone accounts for nearly half of global URLs
insights.locator: Opening paragraphs on AI as a general-purpose technology

insights.claim: Danish is dramatically overrepresented online relative to its speaker base: roughly 7 out of every 10,000 people globally speak Danish, but 51 out of every 10,000 global URLs are written in Danish — over a 7x overrepresentation.
insights.speaker: Daniel Gerszon Mahler
insights.so_what: A concrete benchmark ratio (speakers vs. URL share) that can be used to gauge which languages are AI-data-rich vs. data-poor.
insights.quote: This means that Danish is overrepresented online.
insights.locator: Out of every 10,000 people globally, around 7 speak Danish

insights.claim: Punjabi — spoken by roughly 250 out of every 10,000 people globally and widespread in both Pakistan and India — accounts for only about 1 URL per 10,000 globally, a roughly 250x underrepresentation despite hundreds of millions of speakers.
insights.speaker: Daniel Gerszon Mahler
insights.so_what: Illustrates the scale of the data gap for major South Asian languages — a concrete case for where AI accuracy/nuance will lag most, and where local-language data investment would have outsized reach.
insights.locator: Yet only 1 URL per 10,000 globally is in Punjabi

themes.theme: Causal Link From Data Skew to AI Marginalization

insights.claim: The author states there is a clear pattern: languages spoken predominantly in high-income countries tend to be overrepresented online, while languages predominantly spoken in low- and lower-middle-income countries are consistently underrepresented, causing AI models to be undertrained and less accurate/nuanced precisely in the languages of poorer regions.
insights.speaker: Daniel Gerszon Mahler
insights.so_what: Frames AI's uneven usefulness as a direct, measurable function of web-data composition rather than model architecture — implying the fix is data investment, not just better algorithms.
insights.locator: There is a clear pattern. Languages spoken in high income countries tend to be overrepresented online

insights.claim: The author explicitly frames this data gap as 'just another way that lower income countries are being marginalized,' arguing AI cannot become a genuinely universal general-purpose technology unless languages spoken in poorer regions are no longer left behind.
insights.speaker: Daniel Gerszon Mahler
insights.so_what: A normative framing that ties directly to World Bank development priorities — signals where donor/NGO funding for local-language AI datasets and capacity-building is likely to be directed.
insights.quote: This is just another way that lower income countries are being marginalized.
insights.locator: Because of this discrepancy, AI is undertrained in languages

insights.claim: The author's prescribed fix is 'deliberate investment,' specifically expanding text data availability in underrepresented languages and supporting local AI development capacity in low- and middle-income countries.
insights.speaker: Daniel Gerszon Mahler
insights.so_what: Identifies a concrete investable gap: local-language text-data creation and local AI-development capacity building in emerging markets.
insights.quote: Closing this gap will require deliberate investment, including expanding text data in underrepresented languages and supporting local AI development capacity.
